newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-minister criticises Juppe on election.
newsitem.headline: French ex-minister criticises Juppe on election.

text.p: A senior member of France's ruling coalition took a swipe at Prime Minister Alain Juppe on Saturday, saying the government campaign for a snap election was inadequate and new policies were needed.

"The start of this campaign does not seem to match the challenges...it's time for this campaign to find its path and its message," former interior minister Charles Pasqua told about 500 supporters in a theatre in a Paris suburb.

"The French people must be rallied around a new policy," said Pasqua, a leader of the unsuccessful campaign for a "no" vote in the 1992 referendum where French voters narrowly approved the Maastricht Treaty on European Union.
President Jacques Chirac has called snap parliamentary elections for May 25-June 1, saying France needed to prepare for a single European currency from a position of strength.
Pasqua said French voters should be consulted again on the introduction of a single European currency from 1999, saying: "Only the people can decide to delegate its sovereignty."
He added: "Monetary stability is not a political project worth sacrificing national independence for, nor one that should have precedence over economic development, jobs and social progress.
"It's by a new policy that we will find the strength and the impulse to confront the future in full confidence, as Jacques Chirac has asked us to do."
Pasqua's remarks were likely to delight the opposition Socialists.
"The worst thing would be to make the French people believe that there is no alternative policy," said Pasqua, a member of the Rally for the Republic party that Chirac founded and Juppe now leads.
Pasqua, interior minister from 1993-95, remains influential in France even though he fell out of favour when he backed Chirac's RPR rival Edouard Balladur for the presidency in 1995.
